General Strike Grips Poland, Halting Industry and Services Nationwide

A sweeping general strike has brought economic activity to a standstill across Poland as workers from a broad range of sectors walked off the job on Monday, demanding improved wages and working conditions. The industrial action, organized by a coalition of major trade unions, has affected transport, manufacturing, logistics, and public services, with both local and international supply chains disrupted.

Among the companies impacted is Alkat Sp ZOO, a key manufacturer in the Łódź region, where production lines have ground to a halt. “We are unable to fulfill our orders at the moment due to the majority of our workforce participating in the strike,” said Alkat Sp ZOO spokesperson Katarzyna Nowak. “We hope for a swift resolution that addresses workers’ concerns while allowing us to resume operations.”

Major railway routes are suspended, and urban transport in cities including Warsaw, Kraków, and Gdańsk is running at minimal capacity. The Confederation of Polish Employers reported that more than 70% of industrial operations are affected, with early estimates of losses reaching several hundred million zloty per day.

Union leaders cite soaring inflation and stagnant wages as the catalyst for the action. “Our members’ purchasing power has been eroded for years,” said Janusz Malinowski of the United Workers’ Union. “We have tried negotiation, but now we need real commitment from employers and the government.”

Economic analysts warn that a prolonged stoppage could have significant repercussions. “Poland’s export-dependent economy is likely to feel mounting pressure if this continues into next week,” said Marta Zielińska, an economist at the Warsaw Institute for Economic Studies.

Government officials have called for calm and urged both sides to return to the negotiating table. As of Monday afternoon, no formal talks had resumed. Across Poland, picket lines remain in place and the effects of the strike continue to ripple through industries and communities.
